text:
Seattle's two games with Carolina at the Global Series in Finland ended in two losses, and Jordan Eberle's week matched the trip: no goals, one assist, under 15 minutes in the finale. At 36, more than 1,100 games into his career, he is still a power-play regular, and 7 of his 12 points have come there. A Pacific North Hockey headline paired his name with "Consistent, Competitive," and the numbers fit.

Nothing about his season is a mirage. His shooting is right at his usual level, the luck around him is neutral, and his chances (1.11 expected goals per 60) match last season almost exactly. His 12 points in 18 games are about what our numbers would have told you to expect.

The problem is the team around him at five on five, where Seattle is getting only 43% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, close to its rate without him. Eberle is not dragging that down, but he is not lifting it either. Watch the power play: it is where his value lives now.
